question.text:
The angle between a pair of tangents drawn from a point $P$ to the circle
$x^{2}+y^{2}+4 x-6 y+9 \sin ^{2} \alpha+$
$13 \cos ^{2} \alpha=0$ is $2 \alpha .$ The equation of the locus of the point $P$ is

solution.text: We have equation of circle $x^{2}+y^{2}+4 x-6 y+9 \sin ^{2} \alpha+13 \cos ^{2} \alpha=0$ Here, $\begin{aligned} C &=(-2,3) \\ \text { Radius } &=\sqrt{(-2)^{2}+(3)^{2}-\left(9 \sin ^{2} \alpha+13 \cos ^{2} \alpha\right)} \\ &=\sqrt{4+9-9 \sin ^{2} \alpha-13 \cos ^{2} \alpha} \\ &=\sqrt{13-13\left(1-\sin ^{2} \alpha\right)-9 \sin ^{2} \alpha} \\=& \sqrt{13 \sin ^{2} \alpha-9 \sin ^{2} \alpha} \\=& \sqrt{4 \sin ^{2} \alpha}=2 \sin \alpha \\ \text { Here, } & \sin \alpha=\frac{A C}{P C} \end{aligned}$ $\Rightarrow \quad P C \sin \alpha=A C$ $\Rightarrow \quad P C^{2} \sin ^{2} \alpha=A C^{2}=(2 \sin \alpha)^{2}$ $\Rightarrow \quad\left[\left(h+2)^{2}+(k-3)^{2}\right] \sin ^{2} \alpha=4 \sin ^{2} \alpha\right.$ $\Rightarrow \quad(h+2)^{2}+(k-3)^{2}=4$ $\Rightarrow \quad h^{2}+4+4 h+k^{2}+9-6 k=4$ $\Rightarrow \quad h^{2}+k^{2}+4 h-6 k+9=0$ Hence, locus of a point is $x^{2}+y^{2}+4 x-6 y+9=0$
